A Letter to the Editor.

I
Dear Mr. Editor!
In "Zagl. Tsaytung" no. 17 a certain Mr. Y. Gelbard addressed us in an open letter in which he demands from us an "account" and puts various "questions" to us. We consider it necessary to give the following explanations:
1) We do not wish to enter into any polemic whatsoever with Mr. Gelbard. But we may not allow someone, for the sake of his own interests, suddenly to become "popular" as a "public worker and provider" and thereby to incite public opinion against others.
2) We are obliged to give an account of our activity not through the press, as Mr. G. wishes, but to the organizations that sent us to the assessment commission — and this we did long ago, without waiting for Mr. G. to remind us.
3) Before one asks a question about legal matters, one should first become acquainted with the law, and not raise, in connection with the turnover tax, a question that belongs to the income tax.
4) Not everyone can make use of "force", as the Mr. "public worker" would like; and for a "vacuum apparatus" to be introduced into the turnover tax, Mr. G. must first bring about a change in the law.
5) One may walk out of meetings demonstratively in private societies or organizations, but in an official institution one must have directives from the organizations that sent us. This the Mr. "public worker" ought to know, and if he is curious to know, let him inquire about the matter with the boards of the organizations.
6) Incidentally, if Mr. G. is so convinced that he has greater "force" than others, the road is open to him; but then we shall have the opportunity to put various "questions" to the Mr. "public worker".
Thanking you, Mr. Editor, for the space you grant us, we remain
Respectfully,
Members of the Assessment Commission for the Turnover Tax
S. Lewin, K. Kapłowicz, D. Gitler, A. Gelbard.
II
Most esteemed Mr. Editor!
You are requested to print the following letter in the next issue of your esteemed paper, for which we thank you in advance:
In "Zaglembier Tsaytung" no. 17, in the feuilleton entitled "A Stroll in the Passover Days" by Ben Asuk [?], a question is raised about the money collected on the flower day, which [?] under the name "Yavneh" was intended for the library at the "Yavneh" gymnasium (named [?] after Fürstenberg).
In reply we have the honour to explain the following: for several years there has existed in Poland a Mizrachi cultural society under the name "Yavneh", legalized by the Ministry of Education, no. F 5 § 91.
In our town too, for quite a long time, there has been at the premises of "Tze'irei Mizrachi" a "Yavneh" branch, which conducts various cultural activities among the religious-national youth, e.g. Hebrew evening courses, various lectures, and also a rich Hebrew literature [library], and it was for its benefit that the flower day took place.
Respectfully,
Chairman M. Oppenheim, Secretary S. Himmelfarb.

How Do Things Stand with the Orphanage?

(The children's difficult situation. How long will they go on languishing in impossible conditions?)
At Passover the tiny little orphans held their own Seder; they were masters of their own house, they did not need to sit at strangers' tables, where years ago they used to be quartered. Now they are content, happy; after all they are people in their own right, at their own tables. They need not adapt themselves to this or that rich man; they conduct themselves as they find comfortable, as it pleases them.
We watched how the little company held the Seder, how happy they were with the ceremonies, to which they adapted themselves like grown-up people. It was a joy to watch how the orphan children want to arrange their lives on their own. They have their own "home", their own rules, their own discipline, their own courts; they feel happy in their homely, unique little world.
We looked at the "orphanage", we inspected it, looked over the housekeeping, and one can only marvel. It is impossible to understand how children can be brought up there. That — we tell you — is a riddle. How can one bring up children in the tiny little rooms located on the third floor, and moreover not all of them have their place of rest there; many of them have to go and sleep elsewhere, and it goes without saying that the lodging does not take place in first-class rooms with every comfort — so that with the best will and the most devoted work the children cannot be brought up as one would wish them to be.
Mrs. Szajn, the mother of the little orphans, is simply happy when she sees a person who comes to look at how her children are doing, and when she senses goodwill in you she begins to pour out her heart. It is — she shows you in black and white — impossible to hold out any longer. It is becoming unbearable; it is simply impossible to continue the responsible activity they have taken on under the prevailing conditions; there is nowhere to turn, one doesn't know which way is in and which is out, and a heavy sigh escapes from her heart: Oh God, when will we finally move into our own building! What spaciousness that would be! How the poor little Moshes and Sarahs would blossom there. Oh, how happy we would be at that moment!
How do things stand with the building? Why is it not being realised? Quite simply: the town as such takes almost no interest in the institution. In town all people know is that it was decided to build an "orphanage", that it is being built — but how far it has got, what is happening, what the prospects look like, that nobody knows, nor, incidentally, does anyone take an interest; and that is what is galling, because in truth a very great deal has already been done. Those who stand on guard, who hold the helm, who run the institution, know that they are owed much gratitude for their devoted, self-sacrificing work so far.
Today the building has been raised up to the roof, that is, we have the skeleton, which says a lot; but one must not forget that a great deal still remains to be done around the building: it has to be finished on the inside, and those who know about construction work know that this requires a quite considerable sum.
We know that many, many well-to-do people responded warmly and came with their donations; but for all that there are still Jews who can give and have not yet fulfilled their duty. Let them bring in their donations, let them show that they understand their obligations towards such a necessary institution, let them prove to the leaders that they give with a full hand — and that will give the building committee the courage to continue and to complete the beautiful ideal that glows in the hearts of the devoted builders like a shining meteor.
Of course one must take into account the critical situation the country is in, which naturally affects our town too; but one must not forget that this is one of the most urgent matters, which must be realised: first, because it is already nearing the end, when one may not stop with hands hanging down; and second, because it is so first-rate urgent, so simply indispensable, that there are no two opinions that one may not take one's eye off the institution until one has the keys in hand and can say: here is the building, ready to be handed over for the welfare of the innocent little children.
The leaders of the institution must now begin to carry out an intensive campaign in town that will bring in the sum needed for the full completion of the institution.
We believe that those who can give and have not done so until now will no doubt understand their obligations, and all of them, whatever their tendency and outlook, will come with their donations and will consider it a privilege that their money too has been "decided"[?] here.
But should one come up against hard, cold-blooded and obstinate people — with them it would not be so necessary to speak to their conscience, to their hearts, as simply to show them what state the children are in now, in what attic rooms they have to breathe, boys and girls alike; that would be the best propaganda to soften their rich, haughty hearts.
After all, no one will be able to agree that in the twentieth century we have done our duty when we let the children be brought up in such cramped quarters, in such difficult technical and hygienic conditions.
We must prove to everyone that we understand differently how to bring up our people's children. One must not forget that for the children of the people one must have more responsibility than for one's own children, because for children entrusted to society the community is responsible, and towards the community society must always bear more responsibility than towards individuals.
And therefore let the community remember[?] that the children are society's children, and the people must care for them.
So let the completion campaign now be undertaken with full strength and vigour; let nothing and no obstacles whatsoever stop it — and that will give the courage to carry the campaign through according to the anticipated prospects.
Y. Sz.
Festive Unveiling of the Poale Zion Banner in Sosnowiec

On Saturday night, in the premises of Holender, Y. Preger, Gelblust & Co., the "Hotel Polski", the festive unveiling of the banner of the Jewish Socialist Workers' Party "Poale Zion" in Sosnowiec took place.
The celebration is opened by Mr. Y. Piekarski, who hands the chair over to Mr. A. Ganzwajch.
The latter, on taking the chair, delivers a lengthy speech in which he gives a historical survey of the origins of the Poale Zion party; the speaker also mentions the heroic comrades who fell as victims during the recent events in Eretz Israel. The assembly honours the victims by rising from their seats. At the end of his speech the chairman hands the scissors to Mr. Y. Piekarski to unveil the banner. To the singing of the "Shvue" ("The Oath") the banner is unveiled.
Then come greetings: from the Upper Silesian Socialist Youth Union, Mr. Lipi, A. Hampel, Eng. Zusman, Kraszniecki, Kokoszkes[?], A. Ojazd[?], Miss(?).
Characteristic was the greeting by the alderman (ławnik) of the Sosnowiec city council, Dr. Dobrowolski, who greeted the celebration in the name of the Polish Socialist Party "P.P.S." and the "T.U.R."
Alderman Dr. Dobrowolski greatly regrets that he cannot speak to the Jewish socialists in their own language, despite their having been brought up on the same soil. The speaker is also proud that for the first time in the history of Zagłębie socialism a Polish socialist greets a Jewish socialist celebration. Wishing success in further work, he hands over 50 zł. from the PPS party as a contribution towards the banner.
After the official part, a banquet (no longer proletarian in the least) took place under the "chairmanship" of "Comrade" Yosef Geldberg, which went on until late into the night.

What I Heard, What I Saw

[Feuilleton — Będzin and environs.] Retold by Ben Amotz.
Done in by them “the Turkish way”..
There is a “Beys Yaakov” school in Dąbrowa. The same type of school as in all the Jewish diaspora, only in one matter is there a difference.
— In the matter of mammon — money, that is.
Besides tuition fees the school (printed “scho-school”) also has a certain income from monthly dues — not from the pupils, but simply from pious women who pay monthly dues, even though their children have no connection whatsoever with the “Beys Yaakov” school.
It often happens, however, that the poor pupils are kept away because they do not bring the tuition fee; then the intervention of the “free income” comes in, and the “executions” [enforcement measures] are stopped.
Towards the end of the term all the children received a circular (“okólnik”) — to bring 1 zł. each for the “cenzurka” [school report].
And since the “pani” [the teacher] orders it, there is no help for it; poor mothers could no longer bear the wailing and complaining of their children, and instead of buying something for dinner they gave their last groszy to their children so that they could redeem the “cenzurkas”.
But the school management decided to deal with the poor children “the Turkish way”: it took from them the pennies won by tears [?] and —
— did not give them the “cenzurkas”..
— That is what “Beys Yaakov” means..
“A scholar — out of the society!”...
It is told that among a society of ignoramuses there was one who found a mistake in the Torah scroll: he noticed that “kara” was written with a kuf... When the members of the society heard this, they threw him, the “scholar”, out of the society.
The anecdote came to my mind when I saw at a minyan how a present-day “intelligent” led the prayers at the lectern (a mourner, presumably) and said the blessing “she'asani kirtsono” [the women's blessing, “who made me according to His will”].
When the worshippers pointed out to the prayer leader that he need not say that blessing, he, the intelligent, did not think long, took out a pencil and —
— struck out the blessing...
Favour-mongers..
In the “German” synagogue.
At the lectern — a young lad in cantorial splendour [?], praying. A “full-fledged” [?] cantor...
The worshippers are beside themselves — oh, what a talent! The music lovers of the synagogue concede:
— A true “artist” he is, the 16-year-old, and they boast of him: after all a native son, hidden until now, and suddenly such a “vessel”.
And when we hear and see how the young cantor [?] copies and imitates slavishly [?] every gesture and nusach of the cantorial “sobs” [?] we know so well, we feel pity and want to say:
— “Ema poyzanikes” [?]! Stop it with the cheap favours, for it will be much healthier for the gifted Gershon Leitner not to let himself be led by you; he must absolutely give up the “visits” to the various shtiblekh...
A “man of the people”...
An authentic occurrence. A town like Będzin went to sleep —
— kosher, and woke up:
— treyf...
What happened? Just like that, a story, similar to [—] [?]: the butchers go to Dąbrowa for slaughtering, it is cheaper there; the shochtim go in a delegation [?] to the rabbinate; the rabbinate admonished the butchers; the butchers did not actually resist [?] — not in words, but they rebelled in deed and again took their cattle to Dąbrowa. That is again a loss of income — so what does one do? One forbids. And indeed a proclamation came out on Sunday morning that the meat bought on Saturday night is treyf, the vessels are treyf, etc., etc.
The little town was shaken by the proclamation. The public — or rather, the wives — were in despair and could not decide: “To cook or not to cook?” (The jesters of the generation even say that “pious” women forgot about the ban and recklessly [?] prepared dinner..). And when the clock struck the dinner hour, the butchers appeased the rabbinate and —
— treyf no more, kosher again.
Not all the acts were over with that. The epilogue of the drama was played in the afternoon at the gmina [town hall]. The leading role was played by the parnas Mr. Szwajcer, who spoke in the name of “the whole people” and delivered [?] a monologue entitled “Shochtim and Bribery”...
The “monologue” made a strong impression; the butchers became so “inspired” that they went “out of their vessels” [lost their tempers] and wanted to step out to a boxing match with the shochtim...
— It all happened only because it was “proper” [?]
— A man of the people...
A blockhead of a question..
Plain weekday Jews come and put to us such a blockheaded question:
— The “Agudah” bank held its annual general meeting; we came — they say — to the meeting thinking that we would surely hear there that the bank had earned a fortune during the year — the bank's operations are no trifle! Its huge turnovers!
The report “came” and revealed the secret: the profit of the “giant” is forty thousand gulden.
So the common folk ask this question: “If the Credit Bank, which is an ‘ant’ compared with the ‘Agudah’ bank, had a profit of over fifty thousand zł., then surely the bank everyone talks so much about should have twice as much..
— “Where is the cat, where is the butter?”
We heard out the naive question and promised to give an answer —
— on Pesach Sheni...
The “Harmful One”

[Sosnowiec — satirical feuilleton; rabbinate and Hasidic politics.] By A. Lemech.
(Dedicated to the little informer against the Rabbi of Koziegłowy.)
Rabbi Nachman of Bratslav, in his profound “Sefer ha-Midot”, breathed with mystical truth, says: “The tzaddik is the image of God of his generation.” That is, when a society, a congregation, raises up from among itself an individual, sanctifies and deifies him, appoints him as its spiritual representative, it is because the chosen individual represents in himself, with his higher holiness, with his pure spirit, the bright sides of his generation’s physiognomy, the sparks of holiness of his society’s spiritual form, the reflection of the image of God of his milieu. Hence the veneration of him, as a ray is drawn to its solar source.
But there are sometimes such noble, exalted individuals from whose very essence you can learn nothing at all about the face of the generation, about the face of their generation; but from their experiences in the stormy sea-waves that want to swallow them, from the many stumbling-blocks strewn over their life’s path — precisely through them the true visage of their surroundings, their milieu, often comes to expression. And how paradoxical it is that precisely in the experiences of God’s chosen the shadow sides of their generation are reflected, that precisely a noble, luminous soul brings about the exposure of the coarse, dark shadows of society...
If we want a mirror of such a Jew as the Gaon of Koziegłowy, who is one of the few pillars of Torah in the present generation, if we want to learn through him about his milieu, that part of Torah-loyal Jews, the learned Orthodox society — perhaps he represents them with his holy Torah-[—]? Perhaps with his incomparable, genuinely religious simplicity and innocence? Perhaps with his [—] attitude and his feeling of disgust toward politics and swindle? Perhaps with... But no, his milieu has scant connection with all of the above. Scant... and yet. Acquaint yourselves with individual episodes of the Gaon’s life, unwrap the bundle of troubles that already hangs on his young shoulders — and out of it will leap the [ugly?] figure of his generation in one aspect, at least [misprint “vigigstns”] disgusting and shaming.
Let us first try to do so.
... For years, years he — the young Gaon, the beloved disciple of the Sochaczew Rebbe, who became famous at eighteen with his learned debut “Siach ha-Sadeh”, whom the great men of the generation designate with the greatest and finest Torah titles — for years upon years he held, as a reward for his exceptional greatness, the distinguished post of rabbi in the holy community of... Koziegłowy. And there he lived according to the Mishnah “this is the way of Torah: bread with salt shall you eat... and a life of hardship shall you live.” And don’t think the post came easily to him. No. Before that he wandered through all the Polish shtetls seeking a rabbinical seat where he could sit in peace and continue his Torah study — but nowhere was a rabbinical post found for him. There are “more important” people than he. You will ask further: haven’t we already lived to see an organised Agudat ha-Rabbanim — isn’t it its task to recommend such rabbi-geniuses to the communities? — It seems indeed not... it has far “higher” tasks. But our young prodigy from Koziegłowy committed an irreparable fault in choosing as his rebbe the Sochaczew Rebbe and not ..— you understand what I mean, right?..
But his time came too; every man has his time. Suddenly people remembered that a Gaon of Koziegłowy lives in the world. And do you know where they remembered it? — In Ger-Kalwaria [Góra Kalwaria] itself. That was back when Zawiercie needed a rabbi and the son of a local rebbe was a candidate for the post. At the “high place” they could not look on with indifference. How can it be? To take a rabbinical post without obtaining any approval, without striking any agreement with, with... (the three dots stand for three particular letters, the very first of which is a G) — just like that, simply take a rabbinical seat for oneself and not pay off “there” with some little concession? A [pakhle?], in good faith. And since putting up a candidate of their own was a danger, and one doesn’t like to risk one’s own body (“Guard my soul, for I am pious”), they decided “to rake the fire with other people’s hands.” And where does one find such other hands willing to rake fire? — It was then that they suddenly remembered the Rabbi of Koziegłowy; they knew his holy naivety. This man will let them take his hands and rake burning coals with them. After all, he belongs to a Hasidism that is explicitly “known” in all the political Ger ways and byways[?], as is well known... The game began: suddenly the “high place” began to correspond with the Gaon of Koziegłowy; at the [Będzin?] wedding a “long may he live” was set up for him. With all trumpets and drums they proclaimed: the Gaon of Koziegłowy, the Gaon of the generation... To whom is the Zawiercie rabbinate due if not to such a great one of his generation?.. And our Torah Cossacks began to take up the cause of the honour of the Torah... “Help, the honour of the Torah!”
There were naive people who asked innocently: if he is indeed a Gaon — and that is surely the truth — why did no fitting rabbinical seat come to him? — But naive is what they are. The more important posts one needs for oneself. The Jewish masses need a livelihood.. Here you see: where the post is anyway a lost one, and one need only wage a [kapetshkele?] dispute for the sake of Heaven, for the honour of the Torah, as is well known... for that one can pick outsiders. Take a nice[?] Tomaszów. The “Mizrachi” has an important candidate — one can’t begrudge them that, so one takes the Rabbi of Wyszogród and sends him to the very front... And the humiliations and sufferings he will endure — don’t “they” themselves get pleasure from it?.. And they made a din: “The Rabbi of Wyszogród, a great man in Israel” — but when Będzin wanted him, R’ Mendel related that he is a tiny fellow, he can go walking under the table.. For Będzin he was not fit, and for Tomaszów — yes. Because in Będzin he would have been rabbi, while in Tomaszów he had troubles and suffering, and that one may well grant him...—
You understand yourselves, then, that in Zawiercie the second candidate won, because had there been a different calculation the Rabbi of Koziegłowy would have been no Gaon but merely a “soapy one”; there is no lack of aspirants from their own “cheder”... But they knew beforehand that the defeat was certain, and why not grant him, the Gaon of Koziegłowy, a defeat?.. Why not?
But a war began, a war for the desecrated “honour of the Torah”, as is well known.. What a pleasure it is to be able to do whatever the heart desires, and all in the name of the dear little Torah?.. And it is, God forbid, not for self-interest[?], since after all it concerns a rabbi of a foreign Hasidism. God forbid! It went so far that they came to the verse: “the holy and pure Hasidim who gave themselves up”.. But all for the honour of the Torah! — And such an honest Jew as the Rabbi of Koziegłowy had to suffer and be pressed, seeing how for “his own good” such deceptive deeds were done; but could he believe that “they”, God forbid, did not mean his good and the honour of the Torah? How can one not believe such Jews?..
...Now Sosnowiec. When our Rabbi of Koziegłowy was a candidate there too, the “high place” held that it was only just that he should become Rabbi of Sosnowiec; they held so because they knew that nothing would come of it anyway.., they even pictured a positive possibility that the Rabbi of Koziegłowy would conclude an agreement with the Lipno[?] rabbi; but would such a Torah-honest Jew betray the people who in Zawiercie had sacrificed themselves for him, thereby committing a sin for a holy purpose and informing?.. And all just for his own good, for the honour of the Torah — would he betray them?...
And the one whom the “high place” wanted was elected, for [?] political reasons. But something went unluckily and the conjuncture changed. A possibility arose that the Rabbi of Koziegłowy would take a rabbinical post in Sosnowiec. At the “high place” they were beside themselves: to allow such a Gaon to take the rabbinical seat in Sosnowiec is no good, because Sosnowiec is geographically harmful.. it is of no use to the business.. it is of no use, it can do harm.. Frightened of such a danger, correspondence began from the “high place” — but not the love-letters of former times. They promise him mountains of gold, rabbinical seats (like Tomaszów, for example), if only he will renounce Sosnowiec. Our innocent Gaon does not understand why he should do that, why.. And when he makes peace with a Mizrachist, a “transgressor of Israel”, at the “high place” they boil over completely: how can it be? Such an evil deed? They already put on angry faces and make a racket[?].. We made a mistake — a fine Gaon he is.. what do I know, some melamed there, an adventurer, a money-sucker.. And to the right place there flows a letter signed by many prominent Jews stating that Rabbi Frommer is a blackmailer, “dangerous and harmful to society”.
Yes, at the high place they will also “confirm” to you that he is a harmful one — harmful because of his genius, because of his brilliant Torah erudition. Had he not been such a Mar bar Rav Ashi [printed “Mar tsar Rav Ashi”], he could have been rabbi in Sosnowiec; and here is the proof: for a second candidate, though also an outsider, they bend over backwards, [until?] they had to work it in Heaven that Jan Piłsudski should become premier for a short time, and R’ Eli’ will surely know how to defend the community of Israel, as is well known... Yes, he would not have been harmful if Będzin were not near Sosnowiec and if he were not such a Gaon... And he will again become “useful” when they need him to rake fire, to send him to a Tomaszów or Zawiercie front, for example — then they will tear their caps: the honour of the Torah! Help, such a Gaon!..
Passive Resistance (On the Present Uprising in India)

A. Lancet.
My friend the revolutionary, who shoots at the moon with words and flays the bourgeois skin off the world, is very angry with the Indian nationalist Mahatma Gandhi — what kind of nationalist is he? Doing nothing is no revolutionary act. Revolution must break, burn, set on fire, destroy, lay waste, root out — in a word: revolution must be what it is.
Perhaps my moon-shooting friend is right: revolutions are not made like that; but how does he know it so surely? He can say that revolutions have not been made like that until now, but history has not yet said its last word on the matter of revolution; perhaps a time will yet come when people will make a revolution in such a way, for instance: they will sit down for six days, smoke cigars, blow out the smoke and gaze at the sky. They will sit, because if a whole world were to smoke cigars and gaze at the sky for six days on end, the world would have to collapse. Perhaps there is no match between revolution and cigars; but the essence of revolution is, after all, to break traditions — so perhaps the time has already come to break the tradition of revolution itself: a new revolution, a cigar-smoking, sky-gazing one.
But let us return to the Mahatma. For a good many years now he has been passive; in that time he has dried up, skin and bones, pure spirit is what is left of him. He has, it seems, not yet raised his voice, not said a loud word — yet the British lion trembles before him and, above all, does not know what to do with him. With a revolutionary of action England would have finished in one-two: put him in prison, or stood him in the corner [?] — and that's that. A revolutionary who does nothing is like a huge mountain standing in the way. The mountain does nothing, it is passive. But you cannot move it. It frightens you with its silence, it provokes you with its muteness.
And I picture to myself how millions of Hindus stream toward the Indian Ocean, silent, sullen, with resolute steps and hard looks; they are going to tell India that it should do nothing. Fear seizes the English rulers at such a terrible sight. Shoot? When people are passive? The bullets, it seems, would bounce back from the mute wall of people. And again: such is human psychology, that [?] they shoot only when one shoots back. On the battlefield soldiers will not shoot if they do not hear that they are being shot at from the other side.
The Mahatma has taken a wicked weapon into his hands, and he has taken the weapon out of his enemy's hands. The enemy cannot keep silent, but neither can he speak, and he writhes as if a snake had bitten him. And when the Mahatma reaches the Indian Ocean, he will take only salt, nothing more than salt — but in this small event lies a whole world of protest. A bit of salt is the point that will set India ablaze; for a bit of salt Great Britain now trembles.
I am still arguing it out with my friend who "flays the skin off the world", and I want to tell him about a passive resistance in my own shtetl.
There was a woman among us, a shrew, who made her husband's life a misery. What did this woman not do to embitter her husband's world: she cursed with heavy curses, threw the dishes, broke the crockery and even brought the broom down on her husband's head. A tall woman she was, a thin one, with sharp green eyes; day and night one heard from her house how she screamed and scolded.
The husband did not keep silent either: he cursed back, he even broke her bones — but it helped like cupping-glasses on a corpse. The end was that the husband began to cough; he kept clutching at his heart: something was stabbing him there, deep, deep. So he coughed for three years, until he no longer had the strength to cough, and he departed this world young. With his active resistance the poor man, alas, lost.
The woman was left a young widow and she married once again. The new husband was the very opposite of the first: that one had been tall and strong, and this one was small, dried-up, barely able to stand on his feet. Everyone pitied him greatly: if the first husband, the giant, had gone from the world so early, what then would become of him, the poor weak little man? Nobody had any doubt that the weak little man would not last a year. The woman would surely be marked down as a "katlanit" (a fatal wife), and men would beware of her as of fire.
For a few weeks it was quiet; the woman kept herself within proper bounds [?] — but how long can that last? Again the wild voices were heard from the house, again plates, glasses and pots flew, again the broom began to work on the husband's head. Well, he is done for, his end has already begun.
But a miracle happened: the husband kept silent — took a mouthful of water and kept silent. The wife cursed — he did not answer; she threw the plates on the floor — he swayed over his holy book; when she swung the broom at him he bowed his head. But the worst of it was that he stopped speaking to her altogether. Days, weeks and months he kept silent. The woman was literally bursting with vexation. She had already grown hoarse from screaming, she tore pieces of flesh out of herself in anger — and he? As if it were not meant for him.
The shtetl saw that things were going badly with the woman: she began to stoop, she went about as dark as the earth, she could not look people straight in the eye. The husband for his part kept silent and spoke not a word to her.
The end was that the husband won [?]. Passive resistance drove the woman into the ground. But that is not all: she herself repented before her death; she called her husband and said to him:
— Know, Michl [?], that I have sinned all my life; I beg you to forgive me, for your sake and for my first husband's.
The woman arrived in the other world purified — and that is what passive resistance achieved.
If my friend learns nothing from this little tale either, he will go on shooting at the moon forever,

[Literature — poetry.] By Roza Jakubowicz [Róża Jakubowicz].

Once, when I brought my father his evening meal,
six groats [„groypn“] with a quarter of a pomegranate in the bowl,
and found him bent over his treatise,
he gave me a look with sorrowful eyes:
a girl — if only she will not crave, just like me,
to learn Torah,
it's a dread [„s'a moyre“] —
it can do her no good!
And I — why it had got the better of me [?],
I did not yet know then.
Today, when my son comes in from the street and, finding me writing,
casts a sidelong glance,
as if he had come upon the tango dance in the middle of a working day,
my mother's heart gives a leap:
if only he does not take after me,
— the shadow on the wall frightens me, —
if only he will not be subject
to the almighty spirit,
who knows,
now his soul is endowed like a king.
But my boy says:
— You'll become an old idler, Mama,
on such a fine day,
better come along with me to the sport, to the boxing match! —
Light and Shadow in the Reviving Hebrew Literature.

[Literature — essay; Hebrew literature and Eretz Israel.] By M. Emanueli.

We are witnesses of the great Hebrew triumphal march, of the demonstrated vital force of the Hebrew language. No one will now drag out any more the old rusty arguments that Hebrew is not a viable language, that it is not suited to everyday use, that it is a vocabulary fossilized in the old books and covered with historical dust, that it can in no way meet the varied uses that a spoken language has to fulfil. All these threshed-out arguments have already today come to nothing under the influence of the revival of Hebrew cultural life in Eretz Israel. The Hebrew school network, beginning with the kindergartens in the most remote agricultural points of the Yishuv up to the Hebrew University in Jerusalem. The strong press and the widespread literature, which in Eretz Israel has reached a level that many languages of culture cannot compare with.

The young Hebrew literature bases [itself on] the new life of the various popular masses who have gathered together to build the national home. Eretz Israel has its own poets and prose writers, who put into verse and depict the present ways of life [?] of the most varied settlements and kvutzot, and at the same time draw from the ancient source of Hebrew literature and history, which inspire [printed "igspirirn"] them to creations that are to awaken in the Hebrew reader his zest for life and joy of creation as a member of the new Hebrew society being built now in Zion.

Our poets, men of letters and artists are gathering one by one, all of them, to Zion, so that the spiritual centre has already been created before our eyes in Eretz Israel.

Besides these mighty, refreshing rays, however, many, many shadowy phenomena creep in that accompany the Hebrew revival in Eretz Israel. The formation of a living Hebrew centre in Eretz Israel developed in Eretz Israel so conspicuously and naturally, and drew to itself the greatest majority of Hebrew writers in the whole world, that they, yesterday's diaspora people, became shollei ha-golah [negators of the Diaspora], deniers of the possibility of a Hebrew revival in the Diaspora, renounced their attachment to their old "homes" and began to shut themselves up in their newly won atmosphere of freedom, severing every relation with the Diaspora. This is the shadow that darkens, for the Hebrew reader in the Diaspora as well as in Eretz Israel, the harmonious insight into the all-round life of the Jewish people. The Hebrew reader of the Diaspora, who always supplied writers and sympathisers for Hebrew literature, is torn away from it and from the possibility of further connection. Not only does the wholeness of Hebrew literature suffer, but also the Yishuv, which because of this receives no picture of Jewish life in the Diaspora, since we now live in a time in which the topical and the momentary must be brought out prominently. The post-war years are bringing colossal changes in the Jewish way of life and a restructuring of the Jewish situation in the economic and political sense. These circumstances influence to no small degree also the spiritual life of the popular masses and of the Jewish dispersions. And these masses are, after all, now the great majority of the people. These masses, after all, hold within them the potential forces out of which the new Yishuv in Eretz Israel has taken shape. Why, then, the estranged attitude of yesterday's Diaspora writers, who have today settled firmly in Eretz Israel, toward the broad masses in their "homes" of yesterday?

Frightening enough are the shadows of the Hebrew revival that are noticeable in the Diaspora. It is enough to mention the sad fact that, at the present spiritual conjuncture of Hebrew as a living language and a factor in the Yishuv, the whole Diaspora, and especially Jewish Poland, should be without a single Hebrew newspaper. Every attempt to organise and create a newspaper in Poland fails also because of the disparaging [printed "butldiger", probably "bitldiger"] attitude of yesterday's Diaspora writers, who have already today settled firmly on the happy soil of Eretz Israel. This fact, which perhaps stems from the bright side of the spiritual centre, nevertheless remains a shadow on the wholeness of Hebrew literature. There will be no complete Hebrew revival if the estranged and disparaging attitude toward the possibilities of Hebrew reconstruction in the Diaspora does not disappear in the spiritual centre.

The young Hebrew generation, which is being brought up on Hebrew culture in the various schools with Hebrew instruction, must have the possibility, through a well-edited newspaper in which the Eretz Israel writers would take part, of a further development of its knowledge and of a full Hebrew revival. This will make up for the shortcoming of a one-sided concentration of the spiritual centre.
A Springtime Death

[Literature — poetry.] By Leyzer Shikman.
Through six large, uncurtained[?], flung-open windows
a blazing east paints the sickroom.
Bathing in the blood-red river of the sunrise
are twelve hot little beds and night-tables, set with round
bottles, lined up like soldiers on guard. —
Ugshter[?]. Under quilted blankets lie wasted bodies
with a mute, dozed-off pain,
only empty, lost faces startle your gaze,
laying themselves bare in their naked nakedness.!
From behind sky-scratching mountains the sun slowly [rose]
like a golden, red-hot plate on the blue banner[?].
Broad stripes of pure gold[?] cut in through the windows,
lick those faces as if with words: wake up, night-cripples!
With soft hospital steps the sister of mercy
steals into the ward, and eleven pairs of equal hands
intertwine, and as much as they roll [their sleeves] up,
a graveyard silence pours out in the room —
kneeling down, the young, blossoming
sister has said a morning prayer — —

Only there in the corner, in the last little bed,
lies flat a little heap of bones — not a stir
of the thin, yellowed face on a snow-white pillow
(this is a twenty-year-old black[-handed] worker,
hunted by hunger and soaked with coal dust;
now he lies unconscious with his young, unlived life,
sick with the popular disease: tuberculosis)
The slender, supple sister takes his bony hand
and turns pale as a ... [?].
With mute, dimming glances he calls his neighbours together;
a few crippled ghosts shuffle up to him;
he bids his fellow-sufferer comrades
to share out equally the bit of poverty
that is left him of life — — — — — — — — — —
Evening. The holy sun hurries like a Jew to the afternoon and evening prayers,
the green world, late[?], adorns[?] itself ever more colourfully,
only that worker lacked air — — — — — — —
Small Portraits of Great Writers: F. T. Marinetti

[Literature — literary portraits.] F. T. Marinetti.
The play of opposites is most often the fate of art. Precisely in conservative Italy, the nest of the Renaissance, where everything is drawn only towards antiquity, everything congeals and is afraid of modern times — precisely there futurism found the greatest echo and is going through a process of development. Futurism, which by its very essence revolts against old ways, awakens to a new rhythm of life. Futurism in Italy counts its years from the appearance of its creator and founder F. T. Marinetti at the beginning of the 20th century.
What actually is futurism?
— A doctrine that demands revision and change of the accepted foundations of art, and puts mechanics at the centre of creation and art. Not sentiments, not feelings should stimulate and govern artistic creation, but mathematical calculations of purpose. Art is such a mechanical machine that the poet must handle it like an engineer. Futurism has carried art over from metaphysical foundations to purely mechanical ones. Futurist poets sing not of an abstract soul, but of nervous, steeled muscles and of the rhythm of city life.
Perhaps that is why the threads run from dictatorship to soul-denying mechanical futurism. And so futurism nests in red, dictatorial Russia more than anywhere else.
F. T. Marinetti is a personal friend of Mussolini. And yet — as he recently declared to a Polish writer — he himself fights against political influence on futurism. "At the present moment," he declared, "we are an independent artistic movement and have nothing in common with politics; we are not a special closed group. On the contrary, we open all our doors wide to young talents."
Futurism has not conquered the artistic world — as some at first believed — but neither has it died out entirely — as others prophesied.
Sh. Elide.
From the Book Table

[Literature — book reviews; editorial notices.] "Nisan".
Jakob Fichman is not only a poet by the grace of heaven but also an anthologist by the grace of heaven, a collector — in this field he is a master. All his school books are distinguished by successfully collected material. And now his "Sefer ha-Arets" — it is, after all, a giant work that will be a book for generations.
Is he also a fitting editor? This can already be doubted. The booklet "Nisan", which he has presented to us as an attempt to give the Hebrew reader a little "words of poetry and thought" "that should fill, if only in small measure, the emptiness of the days of hunger in Hebrew in Poland" — is in no case a periodical that would mirror, even on a small scale, Hebrew creativity in Poland. It is a few collected works, often of better value, but the spirit of a periodical is not felt in it. We feel as though we were leafing through a "Lashon ve-Sefer"...
Still, it would be desirable that such booklets as "Nisan" should not be merely a "nisayon", an attempt. There is, after all, a wide field in Poland for a Hebrew journal.
R. R.

To the Jewish Population of Będzin

[Będzin — Keren Hayesod; Zionism.] Jews of Będzin!
Barely a year and a half ago our town greatly distinguished itself by its great understanding of and devotion to the upbuilding of the Land of Israel. The "Keren Hayesod" campaign, which was carried out then as it were [?] under the leadership of our great guest of that time, the poet Leib Jaffe, made our town famous throughout the whole Jewish-Zionist world. For a time our town served as a shining model for all the towns and townlets in Poland.
Approaching therefore now this year's [?] campaign for the "Keren Hayesod", we turn to all our declarants so far, as well as to the whole remaining Jewish population, with our heartfelt call:
Let us not blacken our name in future either! Let our town not descend from the honourable position it has held!
True, we are aware of the colossal change that has set in among us too in recent times, as we have been hard hit by the "national plague", the economic crisis in the country.
We must, however, also [?] take into account two enormously important factors, which demand of us, for the cause of the Land of Israel, still far greater and more strenuous efforts than hitherto.
On the one hand, we find ourselves in such a political situation in the Land of Israel that we must, as quickly as possible and at any price, enlarge more and more the Jewish holdings there, strengthen immigration, found more colonies and occupy ever further [?] and stronger positions in all possible branches.
Only in this way will we be able to give the proper answer, the proud and dignified answer, to the events in the Land of Israel and to the concentrated hatred of the whole antisemitic world.
Only in this way will we also be able to still our own spilled blood, the blood of the fallen martyrs, the blood that cries out to us:
We have given our blood — you give your money! Our blood will give you no rest as long as you have not created a strong Jewish majority in the Land of Israel!
On the other hand, we must repeat once more the great and eternal truth:
We see with our own eyes how the socio-economic conditions everywhere, and above all here in Poland, push us out day by day more and more from every branch of livelihood; our situation is becoming catastrophic, we keep falling into the deep abyss of poverty, loneliness and want.
The one and only salvation for us, and still more for our children, is, can and must be only the Jewish Land of Israel:
At a time when we see ourselves powerless to open the gates of other countries for us, we have the possibility of tearing open the gates of our Land of Israel and creating there favourable conditions for a large and permanent stream of our sons and daughters, who have no future here!
The first condition, however, is a strong and mighty "Keren Hayesod", which is the central instrument for the upbuilding of the country and which creates the possibility of a glorious tomorrow for our wandering and outcast brothers and sisters!
We approach the "Keren Hayesod" campaign with full faith in your warm Jewish heart!
We believe in your understanding of and devotion to our old and holy martyr-ideal!
We believe that our Będzin will continue to strive to maintain its former glory!
We are sure that not a single Jewish home will refuse a further contribution to our life-fund, which builds our home, our great and proud tomorrow!
The Keren Hayesod Committee
in Będzin.

Oneg Shabbat — Torah sayings and remarks on this week's portion (Tazria-Metzora)

[Oneg Shabbat — the weekly portion.] Torah sayings and remarks on today's portion.
Collected and adapted by Y. L.
Parashat Tazria-Metzora.
—o—
a) "And he shall make atonement for her" (12:17 [as printed; should be 12:7]).
The Gemara (Niddah 31) says that a woman after childbirth must bring an atonement offering, because at the time of giving birth, under the impression of the terrible labour pains, she takes an oath never to have children again. After a while she forgets the oath... and for breaking the oath she must bring an offering.
In connection with this Gemara, Rabbi Levi Yitzchak of Berdychiv interprets the verse: "Like a woman with child, that draweth near the time of her delivery... so have we been in Thy sight, O Lord." (The usual plain meaning is: just as a woman trembles and is frightened in labour pains, so are we frightened before You, God.) "Like a woman with child that draweth near to give birth" — just as a woman after childbirth brings an offering for this, because she afterwards breaks the oath, "so have we been in Thy sight, O Lord" — so we Jews weep before God when it hurts us, in a time of trouble, and afterwards, as soon as things get a little better for us, we already forget the oaths and promises. Sikhat Chulin.
* * *
A "Daytsh" [a modernized, German-style Jew] was seized on Yom Kippur in the synagogue by pious stirrings, and he solemnly promised himself to sin no more, to keep his shop closed on the Sabbath, etc. At the end of Yom Kippur, before leaving the synagogue, he took fright at the pious promises he had made, went up to the Holy Ark and said: "Dear Lord God! Surely You Yourself understood that the pious wishes I promised were only under the influence of the moment; You need not take it seriously, everything stays as before... See you again next year"...
—o—
b) "And the priest shall look on the plague" (13:3).
The Mishnah says (in tractate Nega'im) that a priest may examine all kinds of plagues except his own. Because one's own afflictions one does not notice... in others one sees them, and in oneself not.. "A man may see all plagues except his own."
———
Two men came to the "Noda BiYehuda" [R. Yechezkel Landau] for a din Torah. When he pronounced the ruling, the losing party, who was also a learned man, asked the Gaon to show him the places[?] in "Choshen Mishpat" on whose basis he had ruled.
The Gaon points him to the first blank page in "Choshen Mishpat". The other opens his eyes wide: why are you showing me a blank page?
— Exactly — answers the Gaon — just as you see nothing on the blank page, so you would also have seen nothing in the right place in "Choshen Mishpat", because whatever is against you — you would not see it, you would hush it up; such is human nature.
—o—
c) "And the hair of his head shall go loose" (13:45).
There are such communal leaders and kehilla administrators who run communal affairs according to their own will and self-interest. The proof that they make use of public money is when they hide the accounts, when they do not often submit themselves to the judgement of the public. That is what the verse says: "And his head" — the head of the community — "shall be uncovered": all his communal deeds, all his public activity must be open (paru'a — from the expression "for Aaron had let them loose", uncovered), so that anyone can look into the communal bowl.
Shiftei Tzaddikim by R. Pinchas of Dynów.
—o—
d) "This shall be the law of the leper" (14:2)
The punishment of leprosy comes upon one who speaks slander and gossip, because he intrigued between relatives and friends and sowed hatred between them; therefore — "he shall dwell alone": he shall sit isolated from everyone, locked in loneliness. And because his sin came through chattering, he brings as an offering birds, little birds that chirp without stop — a symbol of his sinful chatter. Tractate Arakhin.
—o—
e) "Cedar wood and hyssop" (14:4)
According to the midrash the leper had to bring hyssop, the lowliest grass, so that he should know that only through humility will his sin be forgiven. But he also brought cedar wood, a fir tree, the tallest tree, to show that too much dejection is also no good; one must strengthen oneself and rise up even while being a sinner. R. Y. H. [as printed] of Apta (Opatów).
———
A person should have written on one lapel: "I am but dust and ashes" (I am earth and ash), and on the other: "For my sake the world was created". The main thing is only not to lose one's balance and to know when to look at this lapel and when at the other — and not, heaven forbid, to do exactly the opposite. R. S. B. of Przysucha [R. Simcha Bunim].
—o—
Avot, Chapter Two.
a) "Be as careful with a light commandment as with a weighty one" (Mishnah 1)
Maimonides, in his Commentary on the Mishnah, lists on this Mishnah among the light commandments: learning Hebrew ("and the study of the holy tongue"); so learning Hebrew is a mitzvah, only it is considered a light mitzvah...
—o—
b) "And all who work with the community, let them do so for the sake of Heaven" (Mishnah 2)
Two chairs stand empty in the Garden of Eden. One chair is prepared for someone who works for the needs of the community for the sake of Heaven — no one has yet taken possession of that chair... and the second chair is prepared for a stepmother who treats the children well even though they are not hers. A popular saying.
—o—
c) "Nor can an ignoramus be pious" (Mishnah 6)
An ignoramus does not remain a Hasid, because as soon as a Hasidic ignoramus begins to feel a bit of himself, he at once becomes — a Rebbe...
—o—
d) "Let your fellow's honour be as dear to you as your own" (Mishnah 15)
When Rabbi Shmelke arrived in Nikolsburg to take over the rabbinic seat, Nikolsburg arranged a magnificent reception in his honour, as befits such a great community and such a great rabbi. When the new rabbi was brought into the home of the head of the community, where he was lodging, Rabbi Shmelke expressed the wish to shut himself up in a separate room. Well, the head of the community was curious to see what the rabbi was doing in the secluded room. He peeks in through the keyhole and hears the rabbi talking to himself: "Be seated, R. Shmelke", "Welcome, R. Shmelke" and more such words of honour. The head of the community is beside himself: is their new rabbi, who is reputed to be a world-famous genius, nothing but a fool who talks to himself? And he resolves to ask him.
When Rabbi Shmelke leaves the locked room, the head of the community says to him timidly: Forgive me, Rabbi, for eavesdropping on you, but tell me what it was you were saying to yourself.
— Listen, my child — was the answer — when I came to Nikolsburg and saw the undeserved honour being bestowed on me, I felt great distress. I was afraid of the sin of pride, heaven forbid; so I went into a secluded room and bestowed honour on myself: "Be seated, Rabbi Shmelke", etc. Well — I thought to myself — is there any value in honour one bestows on oneself? It is senseless[?] after all; so why should honour that others bestow have value? That is what the Mishnah says: let your fellow's honour be as dear to you as your own — the honour your fellow bestows on you should be to you as senseless[?] as the honour you bestow on yourself...

Będzin

The No-Confidence Motion Rejected.
Session of the City Council.

At Monday's city council session all the councillors were present (if only it were always so...). The "pintele yid" [the Jewish spark] awoke, and people came to save Jewish honour: not to let the motion of the "Ejnsl"[?] club — to pass a vote of no confidence in the presidium of the city council — "come to the floor".
Around the motion a discussion took place, in which the PPS [Polish Socialist Party] leaders and the councillors of "Ejnsl" took part; the two "Jew-hating" clubs settled scores with each other with barbs and personal accounts, so that the numerous "gallery" greatly enjoyed the "political spectacle".
———
The session is chaired by the vice-chairman, Mr. Erlich. He reads out an urgent motion of the PPS that the municipal (magistrat) officials and city workers should not work on 1 May. Speaking for the motion: Laskowski and Adamowicz; against — the city president [mayor] Michel. With the votes of councillors Kleinman, Lustiger and Hampel the motion is adopted.
With great suspense the motion of the "Ejnsl" club to express no confidence in the presidium of the city council is debated. Henczanczyk[?] declares that, since the aim of "Ejnsl" is only to remove[?] their member from the presidium, they will abstain from voting. Laskowski, Żebrowski and others also take the floor, "settling accounts" with one another. The "Ejnsl" councillors indicated in their speeches, in an indirect way, that "they already regret the whole business"...
Councillor Gruszczarczyk[?] again did not stay "in debt" at the session and said that it was high time the city administration, too, were dissolved...
On this matter the motion of Director Błażewicz[?] is adopted, to pass over the motion to the order of the day.
In the BB camp [the pro-government Nonpartisan Bloc] there is — confusion[?]..
At the third reading of the waterworks budget Dr. Rechtman proposes that the price of water be reduced to 40 groszy per [cubic] metre.
The answer is given by the president, who says that the city administration is constantly thinking how to ease the water question for the inhabitants. For this purpose — he says — all cellar and attic dwellings, as well as the inhabitants without means, are exempted from paying for water.
This week the city administration is preparing a project to exempt some of the shops and workshops from the water charge.
After the budget of the municipal bath-house is approved in the second reading, Messrs. vice-president Rubinlicht, Director Błażewicz and Secretary Laskowski are elected to take part in the congress of the Union of Polish Cities, which takes place this month.
The rabbinate's struggle with the butchers.

[Będzin — community and rabbinate.] As is known, the local rabbinate on Sunday morning declared forbidden (assur) the meat that had been slaughtered on Saturday night after the Sabbath.
As we are informed, the prohibition was issued because the butchers had rebelled in a certain matter [?], and despite that all the butchers took the cattle to Dąbrowa and had them slaughtered there.
In connection with the prohibition, a meeting took place on Sunday at the gmina (municipal office) with the participation of representatives of the kehilla administration — the parnassim Goldsztajn, Klajnman, Szwajcer — the shochtim (ritual slaughterers) and the butchers, who discussed the reason for the prohibition.
During the negotiations something was actually discovered that does the shochtim no credit. It turns out that the shochtim are not content with the income assigned to them...
The meeting took on a stormy character; the air smelled of gunpowder. Because of this the meeting was broken off and postponed to next Sunday.
A new house-owners' association organized.

[Będzin — associations.] On Sunday the organizing meeting of a new house-owners' (balebatim) association in our town took place at the minyan at Kołłątaja 48. More than 50 house-owners took part in the meeting.
The organizing committee explained the reasons that prompted the organization of a new association at a time when such an institution already exists in Będzin. Those present approved the organizing committee's activity to date, took note with satisfaction of the fact that the new association's statute has already been confirmed by the authorities, and declared themselves [?] in favour of founding a house-owners' bank as soon as the association comes into being, so that the association should have a secure existence.
Because the meeting had not been properly organized, the organizing committee was asked to call a second meeting in a public hall.
The association already numbers 60 members.
The torn “domestic peace” in the “Aguda” bank.

[Będzin — institutions and parties.] This [?] Sunday a general meeting of the Aguda bank took place. At the meeting one could see how our own people [anshei shlomeinu] tear at each other's noses; two sides fought, the “Shtayervatses” [?] and the “Shpirmatses” [?], and it ended with 30 persons to be elected, and this “Sanhedrin” will then elect a board.
At the item on distributing the profit, proposals were brought in that the profit be given to the mikveh, to “Beit Yaakov”, to Tseirei Emunei [Agudat Israel], etc.
—o—
From the Esperantists' association
This Sabbath an extraordinary meeting takes place in the premises of the Esperantists' association, Modrzejowska 44. All members are requested to come punctually.
—o—
[Boxed slogan]
The only solution for our fatal economic ruin in the lands of exile is the creation of large immigration possibilities to Eretz Israel!
Sosnowiec — the voivode's decision on the local rabbinical elections annulled.

[Sosnowiec — rabbinate.] As is known, the date for the pronouncement of the verdict of the Supreme State Tribunal regarding the rabbinate elections in our town had been set for 29 April.
On that day the tension was very great. From the morning on one could see groups of people occupied with the matter.
At midday the special emissary of the “Mizrachi” passed on the news by telephone that the rabbinical elections had been annulled.
The news spread like lightning through the whole town.
The leaders of the “Mizrachi”, drunk with victory, issued a special edition announcing “the joyful tidings” of the State Tribunal's decision.
As we are told, the Tribunal held several sessions on the matter and dwelt above all on the main points: 1) that the voivode, without the consent of the central authorities, confirmed Rabbi Englard as rabbi of Sosnowiec; 2) the agreement between the parties of Rabbis Frommer and Englard; and 3) that Rabbi Englard's brother took part in the elections.
An expensive acquaintance on the train! — A “travel companion” steals 42 thousand zł. from a Jew.

[News — crime.] The Wolbrom merchant Yudl Salcgreber, travelling from Łódź to Wolbrom, made the acquaintance on the train of a pretty lady who was very friendly to him. At the station in Skarżysko the lady went off to drink a glass of tea, leaving her suitcase in the carriage. She did not come back, and then Salcgreber established that together with his travel companion his wallet containing 25 000 zł. and 17,000 zł. in dollars had disappeared. Salcgreber suffered a nervous attack on the train.
Festive Eretz-Israel academy.

[Sosnowiec — Zionism and Keren Hayesod.] The lively interest of Polish Jewry in strengthening and enlarging the work of building up Eretz Israel has found its proper echo in the Zagłębie district too.
This Sabbath the “Keren Hayesod” campaign begins in Sosnowiec under the leadership of the representative of the “Keren Hayesod” directorate in Poland and member of the Council of the Jewish Agency, the well-known speaker Mr. Israel Ritow, who this year conducted the “Keren Hayesod” campaign in a number of larger towns in Poland with the best success.
The campaign in our town will be proclaimed at the festive Eretz-Israel academy, which takes place this Sabbath, 3 May, at 9 o'clock in the evening in the “City Theatre”.
At the academy — in which all Zionist groupings and national Jewish institutions will take part — Mr. Ritow will lecture on the subject: “On the threshold of a new era”.
On Sunday at 8 in the evening the Zionist women's organization “WIZO” is holding a tea party in honour of Mr. I. Ritow in the premises of the Merchants' and Industrialists' Association (Kowalska [?] 2), to which the most prominent people of the town have been invited.
In addition, a series of meetings with the participation of Mr. I. Ritow will take place during the coming week.
—o—
[Boxed slogan]
Brick to brick, colony to colony, factory to factory, from the kindergarten to the university and from the camps. By pioneers and immigrants the Jewish Eretz Israel will be built up!
City council session broken off.

[Sosnowiec — city council.] At Tuesday's session the PPS (Polish Socialist Party) group made a motion about celebrating the holiday of the 1st of May. Because the motion attacked the government, the councillors of the “Eygnl” [?] group left the session.
The Jewish councillors and others did the same; no quorum remained and the session was broken off.
Conference of the “Gemilut Hesed” (free-loan) funds.

[Sosnowiec — free-loan funds.] Next Sunday a conference will take place here with the participation of delegates of the “Gemilut Hesed” funds in Zagłębie and the surrounding small towns in the Kielce voivodeship.
The directors of the “Joint” — Messrs. Kahan, Szwajcer, Giterman — are also to take part in the conference.
The distinguished guests will at the same time acquaint themselves with the actual situation of the funds in Zagłębie.
Verdict in the Communists' Trial

[Zagłębie — courts, communists.]
Verdict in the communists' trial.
The sensational trial of 25 persons who sat in the dock for communist activity was concluded this Monday.
Sentenced were: St. Warwa[?] to 4 years; A. Rozenkranc, Kowalczyk and Rivka Malgowicer to 3 years; Rosławski and Orgasz[?] to 2 years; Yaakov Gewirtzman[?], Fela Malnowicer[?], B. Pachter, Primet[?] Rozenkranc, Chaim Grin, Borowik[?], Filipowski, Sarpatin[?] to 1 year in prison.
The rest were acquitted.
The accused received the verdict very calmly.
House Set on Fire Out of Revenge

[Wojkowice — crime, fire.]
House set on fire out of revenge.
In Wojkowice a fire broke out at the home of a local resident and the building burned down. Suspicion fell on the former landlord, who had sold the house in 1923 and, out of revenge, burned the house down.
The arsonist has been put in prison.
Increased Activity of “HeChalutz” / Died in the Mikveh / A Flood of Denunciations... / “Hashomer Hatzair” Has a Garden of Its Own

[Sosnowiec — Zionism, pioneers; Sosnowiec — news.]
Increased activity of “HeChalutz”.
Last Sunday 5 chalutzim [pioneers] of the local organization left for Radomsko for hachshara [agricultural training]. A large crowd saw them off on the platform.
Altogether, in the past year up to 40 chalutzim and chalutzot have left for hachshara. Many of them have already returned and are preparing to leave for Eretz Israel.
Soon the organization will carry out a broad Keren HeChalutz campaign. The local Jewish population will surely appreciate the importance of this campaign at the present moment and will take a worthy part in it.
—o—
Died in the mikveh.
On Friday there died in the local mikveh [ritual bath] “Yellow Meirl” [i.e. red-haired Meir], well known throughout Zagłębie; the deceased's profession was collecting alms. Bills of exchange for 3000 zł. were found on him...
—o—
A flood of denunciations...
Rumours are circulating here that denunciations have also been lodged against the rabbis Hager and Halberstam.
—o—
“Hashomer Hatzair” has a garden of its own.
After much effort the local “Hashomer Hatzair” has received into its possession a beautiful garden with fruit trees. Rabbi[?] Frommer visited the garden last week and blessed the trees.
—o—
[Keren Hayesod appeal, boxed:]
Jew! Do you want to secure a good livelihood for your children? Help build a strong and mighty Eretz Israel through the Keren Hayesod!
Dąbrowa — Old Tax Arrears Cancelled / About a “Jewish Public Elementary School” / Explosion of a Rifle Bullet

[Dąbrowa — municipality, taxes; Dąbrowa — education; Zagórze — accident.]
Dąbrowa [Górnicza]
Old tax arrears cancelled.
At the last session of the local town council the municipal tax arrears from 1924 to 1929, amounting to 8,046 zł., were cancelled. This sum was owed by no fewer than[?] 938 taxpayers...
—o—
About a “Jewish public elementary school” [szkoła powszechna].
This week Councillor Renpic[?] conferred with the school inspector Mr. Lichowski[?] of Sosnowiec about opening, in the new school year, a public elementary school for the local Jewish children.
The inspector declared that he doubts whether the project can be realised in the new school year. Nevertheless — he added — the Jewish community [gmina] must stay on the alert and press on, so that the school is opened as soon as possible.
—o—
Explosion of a rifle bullet.
A group of children in Zagórze found a rifle bullet in the field. While they were playing with the find, the bullet exploded and inflicted several severe wounds on one boy.
Clashes between police and demonstrators on 1 May in Zagłębie

Yesterday passed relatively quietly. The P.P.S. [Polish Socialist Party], together with the Right „Poale Zion“ and „Frayhayt“ [its youth movement], held meetings and demonstrated.

In Dąbrowa and in Sosnowiec it came to bloody clashes between the police and Communists; the demonstrators threw stones at the police, the latter defended themselves with firearms [?], and many, among them the Communist deputy Rożek, were wounded.

As the crowd was dispersing, the shop windows of Grabowski, Weinreb [?] and Rechnitz [?] in Dąbrowa were smashed.

On Fabryczna [?] Street in Sosnowiec a small detachment of mounted police came upon a large crowd of workers, who attacked the police with stones, bricks and the like. Soon a larger number of police arrived and dispersed the demonstrators; several people were seriously wounded in the process.

In the afternoon [?] it was quiet everywhere.

—o—

10th anniversary of the 23rd Regiment

Today, Saturday, 3 May, the 23rd Regiment in Będzin celebrates its 10th anniversary. In honour of the anniversary the Jewish kehilla has presented an electric clock bearing an inscription in Hebrew and Polish.

It was also decided to send a delegation to greet the anniversary.

The delegation consists of: the chairman of the kehilla council, Mr. Gutman; the vice-chairman of the board, Mr. Prawer; and the director of „Yavne“, Dr. Eighorn [?].

Express Trains Are Not to Stop in Będzin

[Będzin — railways; the new timetable.]
So the new timetable provides.
From the 15th of this month the present timetable will be changed. The railway directorate has this time prepared a „surprise“ for Będzin and decided that all express trains shall not stop in Będzin.
In this connection the Chamber of Commerce sent a memorandum, and the Magistrat (municipality) and the „Merchants' Association“ appealed by telegram about the planned injustice which the railway directorate wants to commit against the town of Będzin, which is the centre of Zagłębie.
It is to be hoped that the directorate will withdraw the decision in good time and not wrong[?] a town of 50 thousand inhabitants.
From the Sosnowiec Artisans' Association

[Sosnowiec — artisans.]
On Sunday, in the hall of the „Hotel Polski“, under the chairmanship of Mr. Opatowski[?], a large mass meeting of all Jewish artisans of Sosnowiec and the vicinity took place, at which a number of important tax and guild matters were dealt with.
After the addresses of Messrs. Dr. Rotsztajn, S. Langer, S. Sztern, A. Gancwajch, Ch. Gawryłowicz and others, a unanimous resolution was adopted, expressing recognition of and confidence in the present leadership of the Artisans' Association for its devoted work on behalf of the interests of Jewish artisans in Sosnowiec.
This Saturday night (motzei Shabbat) a pre-election meeting will take place in the association's own premises, in connection with the general meeting of the Artisans' and Small Traders' Bank, which takes place next Sunday.
Senator Dr. Brojde in Sosnowiec / A Fantastic Children's Performance / Appearance of Distinguished Theatre Guests

[Sosnowiec — education; followed by two short items: Będzin, theatre.]
In connection with the fact that the landlord Mr. Grinbaum wants to evict the Jewish girls' gymnasium in Sosnowiec, Dr. Brojde of Łódź came here, and yesterday evening held a conference with the parents of the school about this matter.
A detailed report — in the next issue.
—o—
A Fantastic Children's Performance.
On the 15th of this month, on the initiative of public (folk) schools no. 4 and 8 in Będzin, a „fantastic children's performance“ will take place. The programme was written by the wife of engineer Szniderman.
—o—
Appearance of Distinguished Theatre Guests.
The beloved artists Ola Lilith, Ch.[?] Gadik[?] and the American star Boris[?] Thomashefsky have come to Zagłębie for just 1 performance.
Tonight they play in Będzin, tomorrow evening — in Sosnowiec.
Rabbi Hager's Lecture / The Będzin Merchants' Association / A Museum in Zagłębie / Last Date for Filing Appeals

[Sosnowiec — lecture; followed by three short items: Będzin — merchants, museum, taxes.]
This Saturday night (motzei Shabbat), in the premises of the Sosnowiec „Mizrachi“, Modrzejowska 18, the great Rabbi R' Menachem Hager will give a lecture on the topic „Eretz Israel, England and the Jewish People“.
—o—
The Będzin Merchants' Association
announces that the office for stamping (calibrating) scales and measures will be active in Będzin until the 24th of this month, on Jasna Street.
—o—
A Museum in Zagłębie.
Today, Friday, a meeting of the initiators who want to create a museum in Zagłębie will take place at the Starostwo (district office).
For this purpose the walls of the castle are to be put in order, and the museum is to be installed in the building.
—o—
Last Date for Filing Appeals.
Next[?] Thursday, the 15th of May, is the last date for filing appeals (odwołania) against excessive turnover tax.
Wholesalers (hurtownicy) who do not keep commercial books must apply by 15 May to the Urząd Skarbowy (tax office) with a request that their assessed turnover tax be reduced from 2 to 1 per cent.
Late requests will not be taken into account.

The Festive Keren Hayesod Academy in Sosnowiec

[Sosnowiec — Zionism; Keren Hayesod.] Last Saturday evening the festive academy took place in the Municipal Theatre, for the opening of this year's Keren Hayesod campaign in Sosnowiec, which is being conducted under the direction of Mr. Israel Ritow, member of the Council of the Jewish Agency and member of the Keren Kayemet directorate in Poland.
The academy is opened by the chairman of the campaign committee, Mr. B. Rosman, who greets the distinguished guest, the delegates of the organisations and the public; he then hands over the chair to Mr. Sencer.
After the short and successful speech of Mr. Sencer, fine greetings are delivered by: Mr. Kupermintz (Jewish kehilla), Mr. Feldman (Zionists), Mr. Gantzweich (Right Poale Zion), Mrs. Rosman (WIZO), Mrs. Langer (KKL).
Then the floor is given to Mr. Ritow, who is greeted with a storm of applause.
In his hour-and-a-half lecture Mr. Ritow analyses the Jewish situation and proves with incisive arguments the necessity of a Jewish territory, a Jewish home; then he gives the grounds for Palestinism — why precisely Eretz Israel. He shows that between every people and its land there exists a blood-bond, and therefore there can be no free choice here. The Jews came into being and developed as a nation [in] Eretz Israel, and when one seeks a way to normalise Jewish life, the life of exile, it is only through the attachment to the "skir"[?] [probably: the soil], from which the Jewish people drew all its qualities and in which its character, national psychology and culture were formed.
Here he passes on to the claims of the enemies of Zion that Eretz Israel can no longer absorb any new immigrants at all and that Zionism is therefore no more than a utopia. Point by point he demolishes this opinion and demonstrates that in Eretz Israel there is still room for millions of new immigrants.
Finally he dwells on the means needed for the upbuilding of Eretz Israel. People and capital are needed. People we have — the best human material one can possibly imagine, for which all the peoples of the world envy us; but we lack capital. And here the people has shown all its backwardness. Had we really wanted to give, during the first "five years, 25 million pounds to the Keren Hayesod — as had been planned — we would perhaps already be close to our goal. And what are 25 million pounds for a Jewish people of 17 million?!
The speaker warns of the great responsibility which the present moment places upon all of us, and ends with a vision of the future Eretz Israel, when we shall all render an account before our history. "I wish you," he concludes, "that you will not have to be ashamed of your account."
When Mr. Ritow finished his speech a long ovation broke out. The speech was a rare oratorical masterpiece. For the hour and a half the audience sat as if riveted to their seats and as if enchanted by the music of oratory. The speech was interwoven with brilliant ideas, scientific formulas, flashing witticisms; in spite of the fine humour often used, the speech was breathed through with a deep seriousness. At times the speaker carried the listeners away mightily with his wonderful pathos.
The speech left a powerful impression. Let us hope that this impression will accompany the whole campaign, which has every prospect of success.
N. N.

Dear Mr. Editor!
I ask you kindly to publish in the next issue of your esteemed paper the following open letter to the Jewish kehilla administration in Będzin, for which I express to you my best thanks.
To the administration of the Jewish kehilla in Będzin.
Regarding your letter in the "Zaglembier Tsaytung" no. 17, I have the honour first of all to point out to you that whoever, whoever, but not you, Mr. Prawer[?], should have given such an answer; I had reckoned that you remember the saying "and know what to answer"...

II
We politely ask the esteemed editors to publish in your esteemed paper the following fact, which characterises the activity, the "holy heroics", of the local shochtim (ritual slaughterers).
For a long time the administration of the local gmina (community) has suspected the shochtim of not contenting themselves with the salary paid by the gmina.
The administration investigated the matter thoroughly and finally got on the trail, but the "shochtim's voice"[?] does not give in so quickly; therefore the gmina adopted a resolution to hand the matter over to the rabbinate, so that they would rule on it. This was supposed to happen still before Passover. Last week the rabbinate officially announced that they refuse to rule on this matter (honest people, after all). So the council and the administration, together with the rabbinate, adopted at their last meeting a resolution to impose on the shochtim a "temporary removal" (suspension) for 3 weeks. The date for carrying out the ruling was left to the discretion of the administration.
It is worth noting that since the present term of office this is already the second established fact of this kind.
We thank you in advance and sign with respect,
The administration of the Hebrew kehilla in Bibirca[?] (possibly Zawiercie).
